title: Connected fibres from formal functions and idempotents
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be proper, and assume $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=R$. Then every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), lines 15334--15357; the formal-functions input is Cohomology Lemma 30.4.1 (Tag 02OD), and the proper-fibre idempotent input is Derived Categories Lemma 21.16.1 (Tag 0G7X)

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-stein-universally-closed-factor] to obtain surjectivity of q = X.toSpecΓ and invertibility of its sharp map. The normalization hypothesis makes f.steinFactorizationBase an isomorphism. By f = q composed with this isomorphism, f is surjective and all section maps f.app U are isomorphisms. The fibre homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] transfers a preimage of s to a point of the scheme-theoretic fibre.

source.place: Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), normalized affine reduction and final idempotent argument; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2

proof.text: For any clopen subset V of the fibre, use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-clopen-idempotent] to choose its characteristic idempotent e. By [lem-weil-pbc-stein-fibre-idempotent-image], e is the restriction of a section t over the inverse image of an open neighbourhood U of s. Invert f.app U to obtain the base section a with f.app U a = t. No idempotence of t or a is needed.

source.place: Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), normalized affine reduction and final idempotent argument; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2

proof.text: The canonical map k : Spec κ(s) to the base has image s by [def-weil-residue-field], hence its inverse image of U is the whole spectrum. Pull a back to a global section b of Spec κ(s). The Cartesian fibre identity of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and functoriality of appLE show e = g.appTop b for g the fibre projection to Spec κ(s). Through ΓSpecIso, b corresponds to an element of the field κ(s), so b is zero or a unit. Its image e is therefore zero or a unit; an idempotent unit equals one. Thus e is zero or one and V is empty or the whole fibre. Together with nonemptiness, the topological clopen criterion gives ConnectedSpace.
